original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $A = k[[x_1, \ldots, x_n]]$. Let
$I = (f_1, \ldots, f_m) \subset A$ be an ideal. For any
$r \geq 0$ the ideal in $A/I$ generated by the $r \times r$-minors
of the matrix $(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)$ is independent
of the choice of the generators of $I$ or the
regular system of parameters $x_1, \ldots, x_n$ of $A$.

final_content.statement:
Let $k$ be a field. A proper curve over $k$ is a proper integral $k$-scheme of Krull dimension one; a proper $k$-scheme of dimension one need not be integral. For any proper such scheme $X$ with $H^0(X,\mathcal O_X)=k$, define its genus as $g(X)=\dim_k H^1(X,\mathcal O_X)$. If $X$ is one-dimensional, Cohen–Macaulay and equidimensional, its coherent dualizing module is $\omega_X=H^{-1}(f^!k)$ for $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; it is invertible when $X$ is Gorenstein.

For a Noetherian local $k$-algebra $(A,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$, the residue field extension is separable when $\kappa/k$ is separable. A nondegenerate binary quadratic form $q=au^2+buv+cv^2$ has invertible polar bilinear form (matrix $\begin{pmatrix}2a&b\\b&2c\end{pmatrix}$), and $\kappa[[u,v]]/(q)$ is the completed local model of a node. For a finitely presented module $M$ with presentation $R^m\to R^n\to M\to0$, its first Fitting ideal $\operatorname{Fitt}_1(M)$ is generated by the $(n-1)$-minors of the presenting matrix; for $M=\Omega_{X/k}$ this defines a closed subscheme of the singular locus. The number of geometric branches and $\delta$-invariant of a one-dimensional local ring are computed after normalization and separable closure of residue fields.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic
$k$-scheme of dimension $1$. Let $Y \to X$ be an \'etale morphism.
Let $y \in Y$ be a point with image $x \in X$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $x$ is a closed point of $X$ and a node, and
\item $y$ is a closed point of $Y$ and a node.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lemma-facts-about-nodal-curves}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme
equidimensional of dimension $1$ whose singularities are at-worst-nodal.
Then $X$ is Gorenstein and geometrically reduced.

Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a locally algebraic $k$-scheme
equidimensional of dimension $1$ whose singularities are at-worst-nodal.
If $Y \subset X$ is a reduced closed subscheme
equidimensional of dimension $1$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the singularities of $Y$ are at-worst-nodal, and
\item if $Z \subset X$ is the scheme theoretic closure of
$X \setminus Y$, then
\begin{enumerate}
\item the scheme theoretic intersection $Y \cap Z$ is
the disjoint union of spectra of finite separable extensions of $k$,
\item each point of $Y \cap Z$ is a node of $X$, and
\item $Y \to \operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is smooth at every point of $Y \cap Z$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
